prompt: The client wants to know why profit fell from 2023 to 2025. Which takeaway matters most?

exhibit.title: Revenue and cost of goods sold ($M)

options.text: COGS grew faster than revenue, cutting gross profit
options.feedback: Right. COGS rose 25% (120 to 150) against 10% revenue growth (200 to 220), so gross profit fell from 80 to 70.

options.text: Revenue grew 10% over the period, reaching $220M in 2025
options.feedback: True, but growing revenue doesn't explain why profit fell. Look at what grew faster.

options.text: Revenue dipped in 2025 while the cost of goods rose
options.feedback: Revenue rose every year, from 200 to 220.

options.text: Supplier contracts pushed up the cost of goods sold
options.feedback: The chart shows costs rising, not why. A supplier contract may be true, but nothing here supports it.

explanation: COGS rose 25% (120 to 150) against 10% revenue growth (200 to 220), so gross profit fell from 80 to 70.

extras.proof: COGS rose 25% (120 to 150) against 10% revenue growth (200 to 220), so gross profit fell from 80 to 70.
